step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram depicts a Magento-based e-commerce platform hosted on AWS. Request routing starts at Route 53, passing through AWS WAF to CloudFront. CloudFront directs static traffic to S3 and web traffic to a load balancer running on an EC2 instance (Pass Secure). The load balancer forwards requests to an Amazon EKS cluster hosting the application containers. EKS connects to multiple backend components: OpenSearch (labeled ElasticSearch) for search indexing, ElastiCache for caching/sessions, an EC2 instance acting as an NFS server, Aurora MySQL database, and S3 for logs/static storage. Below the main visual graph, four standalone components are drawn without explicit arrow connections: VPN, Lambda, Redshift, and an EC2 instance (mail server).
